samples.summary: `cells batch` stdin branch and its ' on stdin' error message have no test
samples.evidence: cells.ts was restructured so the stdin read + JSON.parse sit in a new try that produces `Invalid JSON cell data on stdin: …`. The new packages/cli/test/cells.test.ts opens with a docblock claiming coverage of "JSON from `--data`/stdin", but every case passes `--data`; the only message asserted is `'Invalid JSON cell data in --data'` (cells.test.ts:70). Nothing drives the `for await (const chunk of process.stdin)` path, so a broken stdin read or a wrong branch label ships green. Other suites in this repo do stub stdin (docs-import.test.ts:200, notes-import.test.ts:120), so this is achievable.

samples.summary: Vacuous assertion in the sheets-export round-trip test (`not.toContain("'-7")`)
samples.evidence: The fixture cell value is `'-7'`, and `neutralizeFormula` explicitly exempts plain signed numbers via PLAIN_NUMBER (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:12-16). So `expect(written).not.toContain("'-7")` holds whether `neutralizeFormulas` is true or false — it cannot fail if the export option is flipped back. Only the `not.toContain("'=SUM(B2:B100)")` assertion actually pins the new behavior; a fixture value like `@SUM(A1)` or a leading `=` text cell would add real signal.

samples.summary: New CSV quoting rule (\r, \t) is only tested on the neutralizing path, not on the export/interchange path
samples.evidence: NEEDS_QUOTING now quotes `\r` and `\t`, which changes bytes written by `sheets export` too (formatCsv(..., { neutralizeFormulas: false }), sheets-export.ts:52). output.test.ts only exercises the new quoting with `{ neutralizeFormulas: true }` (output.test.ts, 'quotes control characters so a value cannot forge a new record'), and sheets-export.test.ts uses only benign values. The comment in sheets-export.ts claims an export→import round trip, but no test round-trips the written file back through `parseCsv`/`sheets import`, so the interchange claim is unverified.

samples.summary: `--format`-before-request ordering untested for docs/notes/slides/cells/sheets-import, including destructive deletes
samples.evidence: The diff adds `parseOutputFormat` ahead of the request in 20+ call sites, and pins the ordering with dedicated tests only for files (files-format.test.ts), tabs (tabs.test.ts), api-keys (api-keys.test.ts), status/ctx/schema (status.test.ts). `docs delete` (docs.ts:159), `notes delete` (notes.ts:121), `slides delete` (slides.ts:126), `cells set/delete/batch` (cells.ts:63,96,158) and `sheets import` (sheets-import.ts:50) have no equivalent assertion that the request is not made — the same defect the change exists to prevent could regress there unnoticed.

samples.summary: Updated `status` schema entry is not pinned to the actual `buildStatus` payload
samples.evidence: registry.ts now advertises loggedIn/message/user/email/server/workspaceId/workspaceName/session/expiresAt for `status`, and ctx.list advertises {id,name,active}. status.test.ts asserts the payload shape and schema.test.ts asserts registry names/safety, but nothing compares the registry `response` keys to the keys `buildStatus`/`buildWorkspaceList` actually emit, so the documented agent contract can silently drift from the implementation again.

samples.summary: Near-tautological test: JSON round-trip of a plain object
samples.evidence: 'is JSON-parseable as emitted by the default format' asserts `JSON.parse(format(rows,'json'))` equals `rows`. That holds for any plain JSON-safe value regardless of `buildWorkspaceList`'s behavior, so it adds no signal beyond the adjacent shape assertions.

samples.summary: `notes export` / `slides export` `--format` rejection (message changed) has no test
samples.evidence: The messages changed from `Only "md"/"pptx" is supported.` to InvalidFormatError's `Use one of: md.` / `Use one of: pptx.`. Grepping packages/cli for `Only "` / `is supported` finds only tabs' tab-type message and skill docs — no test asserts either export command's format rejection, so neither the old nor the new message (nor the new INVALID_FORMAT code on those paths) is covered.

searchedFor: grep 'registerLoginCommand|mode=cli|nonce=' across packages/cli (only src hits, no test hits)
glob of packages/cli/test/*.test.ts for a login-command-level test
finding.summary: No test covers the `login` action wiring: that the nonce placed in the OAuth URL is the same one bound to the callback server
finding.evidence: login.test.ts only imports and exercises `createLoginNonce`, `nonceMatches` and `startCallbackServer` directly. The action handler at login.ts:34-40 generates the nonce, passes it to `startCallbackServer(nonce)` and interpolates it into `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}&nonce=${nonce}` — that is the whole security contract of the change, and the failure mode it guards against (two different nonces, or the query key spelled differently from what `github-auth.guard.ts` reads via `req.query?.nonce`) leaves every helper test green while every real login is refused for the full timeout. The backend side explicitly added `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` with a comment that the wiring must be pinned because the helper tests hand the nonce in directly; the CLI side of the same wiring got no equivalent test.

verdict.reason: A test covering exactly the claimed-missing wiring exists in a sibling file the reviewer did not open: packages/cli/test/login-command.test.ts. It runs the real login action (createProgram() + registerLoginCommand + program.parseAsync(['--server', SERVER, 'login']) at lines 83-94), so createLoginNonce(), startCallbackServer(nonce) and the URL template at login.ts:34-40 all execute for real; only `open`, `session.js` and `fetch` are stubbed as external stand-ins. The first case (lines 134-168) asserts the OAuth URL's pathname /auth/github, mode=cli, port>0 and the nonce under the exact query key the backend guard reads (/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/), then drives a genuine loopback fetch to 127.0.0.1:${port}/callback with the nonce taken from that URL, asserting 200 plus the exchange body — so two different nonces or a differently spelled key would fail it. The second case (lines 170-196) pins the negative half: a forged constant nonce gets 403 and never reaches the exchange. The refusal race (lines 86-93, 115-123) converts the 30s-hang failure mode into a named failure. vitest.config.ts:5 includes test/**/*.test.ts, so the file runs. The finding's premise that only helper-level tests exist is false.
